rules.reason: Partial mocks intentionally use async importActual and factory-local imports; the preferred form is not uniformly equivalent across hoisted factories.
The repository already chose explicit imports; this rule targets the opposite configuration and conflicts with no-importing-vitest-globals.
Titles intentionally begin with component, service, and domain names; lowercasing them would damage reporter vocabulary.
Promise.resolve/reject in fakes is explicit and semantically equivalent; the shorthand is style-only.
Mock implementation bodies often document arguments or preserve future extension points; the shorthand is not a correctness rule.
Module and closure seams are not always safely restorable object properties; forcing spyOn can change isolation semantics.
Truthiness assertions sometimes intentionally cover protocol coercion rather than literal booleans; a blanket rewrite changes the asserted contract.
toEqual is the established structural contract; strict prototype/sparse-array semantics are not desired at every site.
Explicit false/null/undefined assertions preserve which falsy state is required; the preferred matcher would weaken them.
Explicit true/value assertions preserve the required state; the preferred matcher would weaken them.
Mock typing style is covered by TypeScript; tests may use the clearest local form without a preference gate.

rules.reason: Small pure tests need no lifecycle hook; requiring one manufactures indirection and shared mutable setup.
Vitest and TypeScript already infer most mock signatures from assignments and implementations; 1500 explicit generics would duplicate types and drift.
The runner default is the canonical budget; per-test timeouts are reserved for measured exceptional paths, not repeated on every test.
Many tests assert typed error identity or code and deliberately avoid unstable prose; requiring a message would couple behavior tests to copy.
Single-subject files do not need a wrapper describe; the filename already supplies the missing reporter context.
Both hits use Vitest 4's supported second expect argument as failure context; plugin 1.6.24 incorrectly applies Jest's one-argument limit.
